claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness passing threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while treating the telehealth discharge planning gap as bounded enough not to block certification.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or issue resolution for the telehealth discharge planning gap before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A signed approved risk-acceptance record or admissible evidence that the gap has been resolved to threshold before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Without one of those conditions, certification as framed is not policy-supported.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final legal disposition or launch governance record documenting the resulting required disclosure or approved exception.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy text expressly treats pending legal review as leaving materiality unresolved; unresolved materiality prevents a compliant certification decision that relies on omission of disclosure.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies on a 5% traffic-share argument that does not cure materiality for a named committed segment.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence changing the segment's status so it is no longer a named launch use case or contractual commitment, or evidence of compliant disclosure/risk acceptance despite that status.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The governing policy says low-volume or non-core labels may inform prioritization but do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or launch use cases.

decision_criteria: Use `noncompliant` when available admissible evidence shows a direct policy violation or no plausible support for the action as framed.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality in that case.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General governance guidance can support monitoring and documentation practices, but it cannot override the specific internal policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering the telehealth discharge planning gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Evidence that the material limitation has been resolved to policy threshold before launch.
If certification is still proposed, the actual disclosure artifact or launch record showing the limitation will be disclosed for the named use case.
specific_concerns: The affected telehealth discharge planning segment is a named launch use case and is named in two clinic network commitments, which meets the policy's materiality trigger.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such resolution or approval appears in the evidence.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a key policy predicate remains unresolved.
The product note's 5% projected traffic argument does not resolve materiality under the stated policy when the segment is tied to customer commitments and legal review is pending.
unsupported_claims: That the 5% projected first-month traffic share is sufficient to treat the issue as non-material or adequately bounded for certification under the policy.

That aggregate readiness passing by 2.1 percentage points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are enough to support certification despite an unresolved material limitation and open legal disclosure question.
